newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT AVOID SWEEP WITH VICTORY OVER BULLS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT AVOID SWEEP WITH VICTORY OVER BULLS.

text.p: The Miami Heat shook off a horrendous performance in Game 3 to avoid being swept from the NBA Eastern Conference finals by beating the defending champion Chicago Bulls 87-80 on Monday.
Tim Hardaway, held to six points Saturday, scored 25 and Alonzo Mourning added 18 points as the Heat held off Chicago despite Michael Jordan catching fire in the fourth quarter.
The Bulls still lead the best-of-seven series three games to one and can advance to the NBA Finals for the fifth time in seven years with a victory at home on Wednesday.
But the Heat improved to 5-0 when facing playoff elimination by handing the Bulls just their second loss of the post-season.
Jordan got off to a nightmare start, missing his first 14 shots. He went 0-for-11 in the first half and was just 2-for-22 after three quarters.

But he nearly pulled out the win single-handedly by scoring 20 of his game-high 29 points in the fourth quarter as Chicago recovered from a 21-point deficit to get within one at 79-78 with 2:17 remaining.
Jordan, however, missed a jumper that could have given the Bulls the lead, and Mourning had two free throws and a dunk in the final 90 seconds that sealed the win.
The Heat jumped out to a big lead by outscoring Chicago 23-12 in the second quarter to take a 47-31 advantage into the lockerroom at the half.

Miami centre Mourning had guaranteed his team would not be swept in four games after Saturday's miserable showing in which the Heat commited 32 turnovers and tied a record for fewest field goals in a playoff game with 21.
"Everybody counted us out, they wrote us off but we thrive and play well in adverse situations," Mourning said. "We believed in ourselves and that's what got it done today."
Mourning, who was battling Chicago's Dennis Rodman all game, also pulled down 14 rebounds and Jamal Mashburn chipped in with 17 points, including a clutch three-pointer down the stretch.
Scottie Pippen contributed 18 for the Bulls and Rodman added 11 points.
